newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa, Mozambique agree on new hydro project.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa, Mozambique agree on new hydro project.

text.p: Mozambique and South Africa will on Thursday sign a memorandum of understanding to study the construction of a new hydro-electrical project which could open the way for the development of a $1.2 billion aluminium smelter near Maputo.

South African Mineral Affairs and Energy Minister Penuel Maduna will sign the memorandum with the Mozambican government to allow Eskom Ltd and the country's electricity utility, Electricidade de Mozambique, to launch a feasibility study into the construction of the dam.
"He is going to sign a memorandum of understanding concerning the development of the Mepanda Uncua dam," Maduna's personal secretary, Fungi Mopshoene said.

Cheap power is crucial for the development of South African aluminium producer Alusaf Ltd -- a unit of Gencor Ltd -- and industry sources said the development hinged on the building of the Mepanda Uncua dam and hydro-electric installation on the Zambezi river.

The Financial Mail reported on Thursday that Alusaf managing director Rob Barbour -- who is accompanying Maduna -- will sign a heads of agreement with the Mozambique government as the first phase of the development of the Mozal project.
Alusaf officials could not confirm or deny the report but said that Barbour was in Maputo on Thursday.
The smelter, with a capacity to produce 245,000 tonnes of aluminium a year with possible expansion to 490,000 tonnes, is planned to be constructed near the Mozambican capital Maputo.
Gencor Ltd chairman Brian Gilbertson told Reuters last month the company still held out hope for the project after a feasibility study proved the smelter to be feasible.
The Financial Mail report quoted Eskom as saying the the first phase of the Mozal project would use 450 MW of the 2,000 to 2,500 MW capacity of the dam project.
